subject: Re: MAP close timeline + price protection / true-up questions
messages:
From: Emma Walsh <emma.walsh@acme.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Greg Foster <gfoster@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP draft + acceptance timeline

Thanks Nikhil — the MAP looks promising. A couple of items procurement and legal asked me to confirm before we move to signatures: 

1) True-up cadence: they want to confirm whether true-ups are quarterly or on annual anniversaries and whether crediting applies to overages vs. under-usage.
2) Price protection window: Acme asks for a 12-month price protection on committed SKU pricing after signature. Is that something Redwood can commit to, and how would that interact with early upgrades or additional seat purchases?
3) Definition of usage: we need a single canonical definition in the contract for what counts as billable tokens vs. evaluation/test tokens. Will the MAP usage buckets (pilot vs. prod) map directly to billing tiers?

We can move quickly if you send a redline and a brief note on the operational behavior (how true-ups are calculated and whether credits apply).

—Emma
Emma Walsh
Director, Data Platforms | Acme Corporation

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma.walsh@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RE: MAP draft + acceptance timeline

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Copying procurement + legal is fine. We can accommodate most of this but want to be explicit on how the economics behave so we don't end up chasing numbers later. High level: 

• True-ups: Redwood proposes quarterly true-ups with a 60-day billing window after quarter close. Overages are billed, under-usage first reduces the committed balance then carries forward as credit for up to 12 months.
• Price protection: we can offer a 12-month price protection on the committed units at signature for the SKUs listed in the MAP. Any new SKUs or materially different capacity (e.g., moving to a different model family) would be priced separately.
• Usage definition: we propose the contract define "billable usage" as succeeded model output tokens plus metadata tokens, excluding internal testing traffic on IP addresses whitelisted and flagged as 'evaluation' in the Console. Pilot traffic that transitions to production will be re-classified as billable based on the deployment tag at the time of ingestion.

Ill attach a redline with exact language for the true-up clause and a one-page operational note describing how credits apply. If that sounds fine we can aim to have signatures within two weeks, aligned to the MAP timeline (can you confirm Acme's internal signature SLA?).

Thanks —
Nikhil Sharma
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme MAP redline strategy (true-up & price protection)

Team — looped you in to get quick alignment before I send the redline to Acme. Key negotiation points they will likely push on: 

1) Quarterly true-ups vs. annual: they prefer annual (fewer invoices + fewer adjustments). We prefer quarterly to keep runrate in line and limit credit runway. Suggest compromise: quarterly reporting with annual financial true-up (i.e., reconcile quarterly billed amounts at year-end). This reduces churn while giving them predictability.
2) Credit treatment: they want full refund/credits for under-usage. We should cap credit carry-forward to 12 months and disallow cash refunds except in narrow executive-approved cases.
3) Price protection window: 12 months is reasonable but add explicit carveouts: (a) material change in model family/perf characteristics, (b) regulatory tariffs or cloud price pass-throughs.
4) Definition of evaluation/test tokens: require a lightweight onboarding tag and console flag; otherwise, ambiguous definitions will cause disputes.

Proposed language snippets in the attached REDLINE_Acme_MAP_v3.docx. Please review quickly — I want to keep the momentum and send back by EOD so Emma can present to legal. 

Nikhil

Suggest compromise: quarterly reporting with annual financial true-up (i.e., reconcile quarterly billed amounts at year-end). This reduces churn while giving them predictability.

Thanks for the draft approach — Acme legal will review the redline but one immediate ask: any language that leaves the definition of "evaluation" to an operational flag could be gamed. Also request an explicit process for disputed true-ups (escalation path + audit right).

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP redline and operational note (attached)

Emma / Greg — attaching REDLINE_Acme_MAP_v3.docx which implements the compromises we discussed: 

• True-up mechanics: quarterly reporting with an annual financial reconciliation. Overages billed each quarter; under-usage first reduces remaining committed balance, then carries as credit for up to 12 months. Credits are applied to future invoices; cash refunds require executive sign-off.
• Price protection: 12 months on the committed SKUs from signature with explicit carveouts for model-family changes and third-party cost pass-throughs.
• Evaluation definition: added a two-part test — (A) a Console deployment tag set to "evaluation" AND (B) either IP-range whitelist or use within an agreed sandbox timeframe. This avoids subjective claims. Dispute resolution: 30-day resolution window + audit right (sample logs) for both parties.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm Acme's preferred signature SLA (they previously mentioned a 10-business-day legal review). If they need longer we should adjust the MAP close date.
2) If you agree, I'll send the DocuSign link and aim for signature by 2026-11-30 to keep the Q4 ramp intact.

Attachments: REDLINE_Acme_MAP_v3.docx, usage_projection_q4.csv

—Nikhil
